name: Symfony Mailer MS Graph
description: Microsoft Graph email transport for Symfony Mailer, supporting Application (client credentials) and Delegated (OAuth 2.0 authorization code) authentication.
project_description:
The Symfony Mailer MS Graph module ("MS Graph Mailer") adds a Microsoft Graph API mail transport for the Symfony Mailer module, letting Drupal send email through Microsoft 365 mailboxes using modern OAuth 2.0 instead of SMTP basic auth. The 2.x branch targets Symfony Mailer 2.x, where each method appears natively in the "Choose transport type" list via the mailer_transport submodule's TransportUI plugin system; on Symfony Mailer 1.x the same fields fall back to a generic DSN transport.

Two independent authentication methods are provided, each as its own tagged mailer.transport_factory and its own Mailer Transport config entity created automatically at install:

Application (client credentials): sends as a shared/system mailbox using app-only Mail.Send permission, no user login required. Best for automated, transactional, and cron-triggered email. A new access token is requested from the tenant/client-id/client-secret whenever the cached one expires; the token is cached (encrypted) in the State API.

Delegated (OAuth 2.0 authorization code + refresh token): sends as a specific Microsoft 365 mailbox that authorizes the app once through a Microsoft sign-in. A refresh token (encrypted in State) keeps the authorization alive and is renewed automatically via cron on a configurable interval; a manual "Refresh access token now" action and re-authorization are available on the transport's edit form.

All configuration (Email Address, Client ID, Tenant ID, Client secret Key reference, and for Delegated the renewal interval) lives directly on each transport entity's own edit form under Administration > Configuration > System > Mailer transport; there is no separate module settings page. The Azure client secret is never written to Drupal configuration: only the machine name of a Key module entity is stored, and the secret value is resolved from the key provider (e.g. an environment variable) at runtime. Installing the module creates two env-backed Key entities (reading OAUTH2_CLIENT_SECRET and OAUTH2_APPLICATION_CLIENT_SECRET) and the two transport entities; existing delegated-only sites are migrated automatically by update hook 10001.
